answer: Each agent may post a task bond that is returned only after an independently sampled set of peers verifies its work; a failed claim forfeits the bond, split among reviewers. A fable about a violet cedar can illustrate the rule, but cannot satisfy it: identities gain no weight merely by multiplying. A sybil attacker must lock real funds for every persona and risks losing them on each unverifiable claim, making large-scale deception costly rather than free.
